title: Move the KeePassXC/Drive/GPG vault bridge out of core; keep the sealed-vault verbs
goal: Vision: V-6. Mandate 84: crates/susi-config/src/keepass_bridge.rs (4,527 lines) leaves core. Core keeps what only touches the sealed vault (susi keys vault status, enroll, migrate-cloud-env, init-cloud-key, exec with its client profiles) in a small vault_exec module. sync, doctor, prime-signing, setup-git, rekey and gpg-program forward to susi-commercial vault <verb> with core's flags, database precedence and passphrase prompt, and name that command when it is not installed. A susi-gpg wrapper without commercial still runs the real gpg. The daemon's unattended kdbx refresh is requested from the plug host on vault.kdbx.auto_sync.v1. Old-against-new runs on one throwaway database showed every forwarded verb's sealed keys, JSON keys and exit codes match once T-CORESIZEVAULT-2 lands in commercial.

reuse.searched: The destination already existed: intellibitz/susi-commercial-apps src/vault.rs carries the KeePassXC bridge as a fork and answers the same verbs as susi-commercial vault <verb>, and its plug host serves the plane bus. Old-against-new runs found four gaps there, closed first (commercial T-CORESIZEVAULT-1 and -2, on its main). Core's sealed-vault exec and client profiles stay in core because the fork's profiles differ. The plane bus (is_wired/request) is the existing socket for the daemon's refresh; no new transport.

limitations: Core alone no longer syncs KeePassXC, diagnoses signing, primes gpg/ssh agents, sets up git signing or re-keys a database: those verbs name susi-commercial vault <verb> and exit 2 when it is not installed, and the daemon refreshes the sealed vault only while the plug host runs beside it. A susi-gpg wrapper without commercial signs with the real gpg but no longer primes the passphrase from the vault. When more than one candidate database exists and no --db, SUSI_VAULT_DB, SUSI_COMMERCIAL_VAULT or vault.json names one, commercial searches its own locations first. A forwarded sync that fails records its --db in vault.json, where core recorded it only after success. Proven on Windows x86_64; Linux (where susi-gpg is a symlink to susi) is not yet run.
progress: Bridge removed; vault_exec keeps the sealed-vault residue; forwarder, gpg residue and daemon bus request in place. End-to-end: forwarded sync seals the same keys as susi-commercial, doctor/setup-git/prime-signing/rekey give the same JSON keys and exit codes, a missing install names the command (exit 2), and susi-gpg without commercial runs gpg. Complete socket 305,757 -> 301,885 (-3,872).
